column2: As printed in this edition, the narration omits wine (الخمر) from the list of things forbidden for sale, and the question reads لحوم الميتة (“the flesh of carrion”) where Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim have شحوم الميتة (“the fat of carrion”). The translation follows the printed text.

On the authority of Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh (may Allah be pleased with him) that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say, in the year of the Conquest: “Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden the sale of carrion, swine and idols.” It was said:
“O Messenger of Allah, what about the flesh of carrion, for ships are caulked with it, hides are oiled with it, and people use it for lamps?” He said: “No, it is unlawful.”

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said at that point: “May Allah fight the Jews! Allah forbade them the fat [of animals], so they melted it down, then sold it and consumed its price.” Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).
ʿĀm al-fatḥ (“the year of the Conquest”): the conquest of Makkah, in the year 8 AH. Ḥarrama (“has forbidden”): has prohibited.
Al-maytah (“carrion”): that which has lost its life without lawful slaughter.
Al-aṣnām (“idols”): plural of ṣanam, which is a kind of graven image.
“He said: No, it is unlawful”: selling and using it is unlawful. Jamalūhu (“they melted it down”): they rendered it.
The prohibition of selling carrion, swine and idols.
Everything whose use is forbidden, its sale and consuming its price are forbidden.
All stratagems used to make lawful what Allah has forbidden are void.
Whoever uses stratagems to make the unlawful lawful bears a resemblance to the Jews, upon whom be the curses of Allah.

This hadith teaches us that everything which is forbidden to eat is forbidden to use in any way, whether attached to or mixed with something lawful, as with hides, or separate, as with using it for lamps;

that however its state is changed, its price is unlawful; that every means to what is unlawful is unlawful and forbidden to use; and that no stratagem changes the reality of things when they are false.
So abandon stratagems in it and be deliberate; / the true stratagem lies in abandoning stratagems.
